results.name: Common_Layers_Final
results.title: Common Layers
results.description:
The Low Impact Development (LID) Infeasibility maps and data products were created for the City of SeaTac by Aspect Consulting in April of 2018 using existing data and LID infeasibility criteria from the 2016 King County Surface Water Design Manual (KCSWDM), as amended by the City of SeaTac Addendum to the KCSWDM (City Stormwater Standards).  The process for creating these layers and the specific criteria used are documented in the LID Infeasibility Study report prepared by Aspect Consulting and dated March 30, 2018.

Incorporated in February 1990, the City of SeaTac is located in the Pacific Northwest, approximately midway between the cities of Seattle and Tacoma in the State of Washington. SeaTac is a vibrant community, economically strong, environmentally sensitive, and people-oriented. The City boundaries surround the Seattle-Tacoma International Airport, (approximately 3 square miles in area) which is owned and operated by the Port of Seattle. 

For additional information regarding the City of SeaTac, its people, or services, please visit https://www.seatacwa.gov. For additional information regarding City GIS data or maps, please visit https://www.seatacwa.gov/our-city/maps-and-gis.
results.snippet: Low Impact Development (LID) Infeasibility common layers consist of a number of products used in the creation of LID Best Management Practice (BMP) datasets.
results.accessInformation: This dataset has been prepared by Aspect Consulting, LLC for the City of SeaTac, Washington and is distributed by the City of SeaTac.
results.licenseInfo:
These layers are intended to be used to demonstrate the extent of infeasibility by LID Best Management Practice (BMP) type on public or private property based on existing data.  Development applicants may use these layers to help demonstrate the extent of LID infeasibility on their property and to assist in locating areas where LID BMPs may be feasible.  It is not intended for these layers to be the sole authority for determining LID infeasibility, and the City is not required to use these layers as such.  

Limitations of use include, but are not limited to the following:

  • Not all areas of LID BMP infeasibility are mapped, and thus additional site research and assessment may be necessary to determine the full extent of site LID feasibility/infeasibility because these layers were developed using existing data and a subset of the LID Infeasibility criteria found in City Stormwater Standards.  

  • Users rely upon these layers at their own risk.  The mapped data was developed from a variety of data sources, which may contain errors and vary in resolution.  The applicability and use of these layers by the City will be determined during the permit review process.  
  • Site specific surveys may be required as a part of the development permit application process in order to field verify the locations of areas of infeasibility because the LID Infeasibility layers are not survey accurate.  The City will make the sole determination as to whether site surveys or other field verification will be required.

  • Neither the City of SeaTac nor any of its officials, contractors, and employees make any warranty of any kind regarding this information, either expressed or implied, including but not limited to any warranties of merchantability or fitness for a particular purpose.  The distribution of these layers and the content therein, shall not constitute any warranty.  Additionally, The City of SeaTac and its officials, contractors, and employees assume no responsibility or legal liability for the accuracy, completeness, reliability, timeliness, or usefulness of this product nor do they represent that the use of the product will not infringe on privately owned rights.  All City of SeaTac GIS data and services, including these layers are expressly provided “AS IS”, “AS AVAILABLE”, and “WITH ALL FAULTS”.

  • The City of SeaTac does not maintain and is not responsible for the performance or reliability of this third party website. The vendor (Esri) may change the functionality or temporarily suspend the site for maintenance without notice.  Performance and reliability are solely the responsibility of the vendor.  Questions regarding the GIS dataset, can be addressed to GIS Support at the City of SeaTac: gissupport@ci.seatac.wa.us.

results.name: Land_Cover_Forterra_2017
results.title: Land Cover Forterra 2017
results.description:
This dataset was developed using ArcGIS to perform a supervised classification on 2017 NAIP 4-band orthoimagery at a 1m resolution captured during the summer of 2017 and purchased from the USDA Aerial Photography Field Office.

A seamless mosaic was assembled for each of the four bands (red, blue, green, and near-infrared) as well as true color and false color composites. From the bands were derived a normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), and two texture layers using a focal window with dimensions of 7x7 measuring the range of values within the window. These layers were averaged to create a single texture layer. 100 training polygons were digitized to identify areas corresponding to the following 11 classes:

  1. Developed/Impervious: Consists of buildings, roads, parking lots, and other forms of urban development

  2. Dry Grass: Grass that has little to no photosynthetic activity due to a lack of moisture and is less than 2’ in height

  3. Forest: Coniferous and deciduous trees that are over 15’ in height

  4. Irrigated Grass: Grass that is watered and has continued photosynthetic activity during the dry summer months and is less than 2’ in height

  5. Shadow over Developed/Impervious: Areas of cast shadows on developed/impervious features

  6. Shadow over Dry Grass: Areas of cast shadows over dry grass

  7. Shadow over Forest: Areas of cast shadows over forest

  8. Shadow over Irrigated Grass: Areas of cast shadows over irrigated grass

  9. Shadow over Water: Areas of cast shadows over water

  10. Shrubs: Coniferous and deciduous woody plants that are between 2’ and 15’ in height

  11. Water: Includes open water on Puget Sound, lakes, river channels, wetlands, and retention ponds.

Training polygons were selected using visual inspection of both true color and false color composites of the NAIP imagery in conjunction with Google Streetview images. The training polygons were converted to rasters, the rasters were used to create signature files, and the signature files were used to generate a maximum likelihood classification, using the R, B, G, NIR, NDVI, and texture rasters.

Vegetation was stratified according to height using 2016 LiDAR data obtained from King County using a vegetation height raster created by masking bare earth and first-return LiDAR data to the extent of the vegetated classes, then stratifying into: grass 0-2’, shrubs 2’-15’, forest 15+. Within wetland mitigation areas delineated by the Port of Seattle, a different stratification threshold was used to differentiate shrubs, with the upper limit set to 30’ to account for large willows within the wetlands.

After internal review of the preliminary classification the decision was made to combine several of our initial classes and to introduce a buildings a class, with the final set of classes consisting of:

• Buildings

• Developed/Impervious

• Dry grass/bare soil

• Forest

• Grass

• Shrub

• Water

Substantial effort was expended to improve the accuracy of the landcover classification. Over the course of four complete revisions to the initial classification, we used King County impervious surface data to improve and in many cases eliminate class confusion between developed/impervious and dry grass/bare soil, integrated vector building footprints and right-of-way data from the municipalities, and hand-digitized thousands of features such as buildings, retention ponds, areas of bare soil, and overwater structures on lakes. We applied the changes sequentially in order to minimize the liklihood of replacing overhanging tree canopy with these features.
results.snippet: Land cover classification for cities of Burien, Des Moines, SeaTac and surrounding area based on 2017 4-band NAIP imagery supplemented with 2016 King County Lidar along with building footprints and paved area vector datasets provided by the cities.
results.accessInformation: Created by CORE GIS LLC on behalf of Forterra for a project funded by the Port of Seattle.
